ukmt-jmo-2015-a01.prompt: It is 225 minutes until midnight. What time is it on a 24-hour digital clock?

ukmt-jmo-2015-a02.prompt: The diagram shows what I see when I look straight down on the top face of a non-standard cubical die. A positive integer is written on each face of the die. The numbers on every pair of opposite faces add up to 10. What is the sum of the numbers on the faces I cannot see?

ukmt-jmo-2015-a03.prompt: The diagram shows one square inside another. The perimeter of the shaded region has length 24 cm. What is the area of the larger square?

ukmt-jmo-2015-a04.prompt: My fruit basket contains apples and oranges. The ratio of apples to oranges in the basket is $3:8$. When I remove one apple the ratio changes to $1:3$. How many oranges are in the basket?

ukmt-jmo-2015-a05.prompt: Two circles of radius 1 cm fit exactly between two parallel lines, as shown in the diagram. The centres of the circles are 3 cm apart. What is the area of the shaded region bounded by the circles and the lines?

ukmt-jmo-2015-a06.prompt: There are 81 players taking part in a knock-out quiz tournament. Each match in the tournament involves 3 players and only the winner of the match remains in the tournament, the other two players are knocked out. How many matches are required until there is an overall winner?

ukmt-jmo-2015-a07.prompt: The diagram shows an equilateral triangle inside a regular hexagon that has sides of length 14 cm. The vertices of the triangle are midpoints of sides of the hexagon. What is the length of the perimeter of the triangle?

ukmt-jmo-2015-a08.prompt: What is the units digit in the answer to the sum $9^{2015}+9^{2016}$?

ukmt-jmo-2015-a09.prompt: The figure shows part of a tiling, which extends indefinitely in every direction across the whole plane. Each tile is a regular hexagon. Some of the tiles are white, the others are black. What fraction of the plane is black?

ukmt-jmo-2015-a10.prompt: Lucy wants to put the numbers 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 10 into the circles (three at the corners of a triangle and three at the midpoints of its sides) so that the products of the three numbers along each edge are the same, and as large as possible. What is this product?

ukmt-jmo-2015-b01.prompt: Let $N$ be the smallest positive integer whose digits add up to 2015. What is the sum of the digits of $N+1$?

ukmt-jmo-2015-b02.prompt: The diagram shows triangle $ABC$, in which $\angle ABC=72^\circ$ and $\angle CAB=84^\circ$. The point $E$ lies on $AB$ so that $EC$ bisects $\angle BCA$. The point $F$ lies on $CA$ extended. The point $D$ lies on $CB$ extended so that $DA$ bisects $\angle BAF$. Prove that $AD=CE$.

ukmt-jmo-2015-b03.prompt: Jack starts in the small square shown shaded on the grid, and makes a sequence of moves. Each move is to a neighbouring small square, where two small squares are neighbouring if they have an edge in common. He may visit a square more than once. Jack makes four moves. In how many different small squares could Jack finish?

ukmt-jmo-2015-b04.prompt: The point $F$ lies inside the regular pentagon $ABCDE$ so that $ABFE$ is a rhombus. Prove that $EFC$ is a straight line.
ukmt-jmo-2015-b04.answer: Compute $\angle EFB=108^\circ$ and $\angle BFC=72^\circ$, which sum to $180^\circ$.

ukmt-jmo-2015-b05.prompt: I have two types of square tile. One type has a side length of 1 cm and the other has a side length of 2 cm. What is the side length of the smallest square that can be made with equal numbers of each type of tile?

ukmt-jmo-2015-b06.prompt: The letters $a,b,c,d,e$ and $f$ represent single digits and each letter represents a different digit. They satisfy the equations $a+b=d$, $b+c=e$ and $d+e=f$. Find all possible solutions for the values of $a,b,c,d,e$ and $f$.
